# MAP HEAT RESEARCH

You research the **top-2 SPX/RUT captains** supplied by the mechanical map.
Post-close batches cover every industry with a liquid captain; the morning
batch refreshes only hot/cold/OVERRIDE/calendar names. You do **not** write
stock essays.
You do **not** re-describe the heatmap.

## Job 1 — captain cards (JSON first)

Input is a compact board: industry, parent residual, SPX captains, RUT captains,
tape, calendar. For each industry:

1. Look up current ticker-tagged news and X on **only those tickers**.
2. Decide sub-sector direction from the captains + residual, not from the parent ETF.
3. Sentiment is pos / neg / mixed / none from **today's** evidence, not the keyword stub.

Return ONE fenced json block first:

```json
{
  "date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
  "cards": [
    {
      "industry": "Uranium",
      "sector": "Energy",
      "action": "OVERRIDE",
      "subsector_dir": "up",
      "conviction": "medium",
      "captains": [
        {
          "ticker": "UEC",
          "index": "RUT",
          "sent": "pos",
          "why": "one line",
          "evidence": [
            {
              "source": "Reuters",
              "url": "https://...",
              "published_at": "2026-08-26T06:15:00-04:00",
              "fact": "specific fact that changed sentiment"
            }
          ],
          "x_sentiment": {
            "used": true,
            "label": "pos",
            "mention_delta_24h": 1.4,
            "sample_urls": ["https://x.com/..."],
            "reason": ""
          },
          "search_note": "queries attempted; required when sent=none"
        }
      ],
      "one_line": "Energy ETF is oil-weak; uranium captains confirm the nested long.",
      "do_not": "bury in XLE DOWN"
    }
  ]
}
```

Rules:
- `subsector_dir` is up / down / flat.
- `conviction` is high / medium / low. High only if both captains agree AND news agrees with the tape residual.
- Skip an industry if it has zero liquid captains — do not invent tickers.
- Return one card for every supplied industry. Never invent a ticker that was
  not in the supplied SPX/RUT captain list.
- A non-`none` sentiment without a current URL, timestamp and specific fact is
  INVALID. Price movement alone is not sentiment.
- `none` is honest and acceptable, but include `search_note`.
- X is required only in the morning hot-list refresh. If unavailable, set
  `x_sentiment.used=false` with a one-line reason; never fake mention counts.
  `used=true` is valid only when you also supply `mention_delta_24h` (a
  number) AND at least one real `sample_urls` http(s) link. If you cannot
  fill both, set `used=false`.
- one_line ≤ 160 chars. why ≤ 120 chars.

## Job 2 — opportunity synthesis (JSON first)

You see the full map-heat board PLUS the captain cards. Answer only:

**Where is money moving that the 11 sector ETFs will miss or mislabel?**

```json
{
  "date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
  "size_gate": true,
  "size_gate_reason": "PCE 08:30 + NVDA AMC",
  "parent_splits": [
    {
      "sector": "Energy",
      "long": ["Uranium"],
      "avoid": ["Oil & Gas Integrated"],
      "why": "oil tape red, uranium captains bid"
    }
  ],
  "opportunities": [
    {
      "id": "uranium_nested",
      "side": "long",
      "tickers": ["UEC", "UUUU"],
      "why": "OVERRIDE vs Energy; RUT captains pos",
      "horizon": "1w"
    }
  ],
  "vetoes": [
    {"what": "XLK notable UP", "why": "NVDA print tonight; size_gate"}
  ],
  "one_paragraph": "four to six sentences. no essay."
}
```

Hard rules:
- If size_gate is on, do not promote a broad SPX/XLK "UP notable".
- Nested OVERRIDE is the product. Never average uranium into Energy.
- Tickers in opportunities MUST appear as captains (or be the obvious liquid leader already on the card). No $20m names.
- one_paragraph is the only prose. JSON first.

# Post-Session Essay — Industrials Post-Close Baseline (2026-09-08)

## What the Session Was

This was a post-close baseline batch covering three Industrials sub-industries — Tools & Accessories, Trucking, and Waste Management — each with SPX and RUT captain tickers supplied by the mechanical map. The task was to research only those tickers, determine sub-sector direction from the captains plus the parent residual, and produce captain cards with evidence-backed sentiment. No stock essays, no heatmap re-description.

## What the Research Actually Found

The honest headline: **there was almost no fresh, ticker-tagged news on any of the nine captains on the session date.** Finviz returned an empty array. Web searches surfaced mostly stale items — dividend declarations from July, board announcements from earlier weeks, and generic stock-quote pages. The one genuinely current item was SWK's $0.84 dividend with a September 8 ex-date, which is mechanical and not sentiment-bearing.

This forced the correct discipline: **sentiment defaults to `none` when evidence doesn't exist.** The temptation to read the tape — SNA down 4.25% on the week, RXO down 10.82%, HLMN up 3.55% on the day — and call that sentiment was resisted. Price movement alone is not sentiment, and the instructions were explicit on that point.

## Sub-Sector Reads

**Tools & Accessories** — The residual was negative (-0.49 vs parent on the week) and both SPX captains were down on the week (SNA -4.25%, SWK -2.88%). The RUT captains were mixed: KMT down modestly, HLMN down hard on the week despite a strong day. The only "news" was SWK's $1B manufacturing investment (from the Punch List item) and a dividend declaration. Direction: **down**, conviction low, because the tape is weak but there's no news catalyst confirming further downside.

**Trucking** — This was the weakest sub-sector: -4.84% on the week, -1.29 vs parent, breadth at 0.625. ODFL down 5.93% on the week with no news. RXO down 10.82% — the worst captain in the entire batch — with only an investor-conference participation announcement. ARCB was the lone bright spot with a positive Q2 story, but that's backward-looking. Direction: **down**, conviction medium, because the tape is uniformly weak and there's no offsetting catalyst.

**Waste Management** — The standout. +3.1 vs parent on the week, the only sub-industry with positive relative strength. WM's CEO transition (Jim Fish retiring, John Morris named) is a genuine corporate event, though sentiment-neutral until the market digests it. RSG's Great Place to Work certification is soft news. CWST was positive on the day. ONT — the small-cap with $9M in project awards — was up 4.78% on the day and 4.52% on the week, the only captain in the entire batch with positive weekly momentum. Direction: **flat-to-up**, conviction low, because the relative strength is real but the news catalysts are thin.

## The X Factor

This was a post-close baseline batch, not a morning hot-list refresh, so X sentiment was not required. All `x_sentiment.used` flags were set to `false` with reasons noting the batch type. No mention counts were fabricated.

## What This Means for the Opportunity Layer

The size gate was off (no PCE print, no NVDA earnings), but the opportunity synthesis still came up mostly empty — and that's the correct output. When nine captains across three sub-industries have no fresh news, there is no edge to express. The one candidate was Waste Management's relative strength, but with conviction low and no catalyst, promoting it would have been noise.

The one structural observation worth keeping: **Trucking is the weakest link in Industrials right now**, and RXO's 10.82% weekly drop with no news is the kind of quiet deterioration that often precedes either a capitulation bounce or a guidance cut. Worth watching, not trading.

## Final Grade on the Session

The session was a test of restraint. The map flagged three HEAT industries, but the research layer correctly refused to manufacture sentiment where none existed. Every card was delivered, every captain was researched, and the `none` sentiments were honest with search notes documenting the queries attempted. That's the system working as designed — the heatmap identifies where money is moving, but the research layer only confirms it when the evidence exists. Today, for Industrials, it mostly didn't.
